title: SWE-Skills-Bench: Do Agent Skills Actually Help in Real-World Software Engineering?
abstract: arXiv:2603.15401v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Agent skills, structured procedural knowledge packages injected at inference time, are increasingly used to augment LLM agents on software engineering tasks. However, their real utility in end-to-end development settings remains unclear, and no standard procedure tests an individual skill before installation. We present swe-skills-bench, a skill-centric, requirement-driven benchmark that measures how much individual agent skills improve performance on real-world software engineering (SWE) tasks. translated_title: SWE-Skills-Bench：智能体技能在真实世界软件工程中真的有帮助吗？
translated_abstract: 智能体技能是在推理时注入的结构化程序性知识包，越来越多地被用于增强大语言模型智能体在软件工程任务上的能力。然而，它们在端到端开发场景中的实际效用仍不明确，且目前没有标准流程能在安装前对单个技能进行测试。我们提出了SWE-Skills-Bench，这是一个以技能为中心、由需求驱动的基准测试，用于衡量单个智能体技能对真实世界软件工程（SWE）任务性能的提升程度。我们从98个公开的SWE技能出发，每个技能都对应一个固定提交版本的真实GitHub仓库。针对每个技能，我们推导出仓库特定的需求，创建可执行的验证器，并构建可复现的环境。在四种智能体-模型配置下，我们对每个任务分别在无技能和有技能的情况下各运行一次，共得到3,920组配对评估。针对每项需求，我们计算配对差值，即性能的变化……
tldr: 该论文提出了SWE-Skills-Bench，一个以技能为中心、需求驱动的基准测试，通过3,920组有/无技能的配对评估，系统量化了单个智能体技能对真实世界软件工程任务的实际提升效果。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces SWE-Skills-Bench, a skill-centric, requirement-driven benchmark that uses 3,920 paired evaluations with and without skills to systematically quantify how much individual agent skills actually improve performance on real-world software engineering tasks.
